title: Partner integration governance and launch notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note collects the governance checkpoints, launch-ready copy variants, SKU and billing guidance, and the minimal technical acceptance criteria for a partner marketplace listing. Aim is to have a single actionable playbook we can hand to a partner PM and the internal launch squad.

Quick summary (for executive one-liner):
Redwood Inference + [Partner] integrated endpoint for predictable, low-latency LLM inference with usage metering and optional private deployment (VPC).

Product positioning options (pick one or blend):
- Developer-first inference endpoint: fast API, predictable latency, and built-in cost controls for production LLMs.
- Enterprise-first private inference: private control plane, KMS integration, audit logs, and SLA-backed capacity.
- Cost-aware routing: automatic fallbacks and quantization profiles to keep unit economics predictable across workloads.

Marketplace short description (<= 250 chars):
Connect Redwood Inference with [Partner] to serve LLMs with production-grade SLAs, choice of hosted or private deployments, and built-in cost & observability controls.

Marketplace long description (approx 150-200 words):
Draft: Redwood Inference offers a unified runtime for running LLMs with consistent performance and cost controls. When integrated with [Partner], teams get an end-to-end path from provisioning to observability: dedicated GPU capacity, private VPC deployment options, and token-level cost traces. Devs can start with a hosted API and graduate to Reserved capacity without changing calls or routes. The integration supports function/tool calling, streaming responses, and model rollout controls so product teams can safely ship features at scale. For regulated or high-compliance customers, the private deployment option plugs into customer KMS/HSM and provides audit logs and network isolation.

Feature bullets (for listing and bullets section):
- Simple REST + SDKs for text generation, chat, and embeddings
- Dedicated capacity & burst options with SLA-backed latency targets
- VPC/private control plane and KMS integration for regulated workloads
- Token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the dashboard
- Automatic routing and fallback policies (latency/cost/region)
- Built-in caching, batching, and quantization recommendations to lower unit costs

Suggested SEO keywords / tags for marketplace:
redwood inference, llm serving, inference platform, dedicated gpus, private deployment, llm sla, inference cost optimization, vpc ai, hosted api

Required assets checklist (marketplace platform):
- 1 x 1024x1024 PNG logo (transparent)
- 1 x 1280x720 screenshot (dashboard: cost per request/time series)
- 3 x 1200x627 feature images (supported workflows: hosted, dedicated, private)
- 30–90s product video (mp4, captions optional)
- Legal: partner MSA or marketplace-approved addendum (PDF)
- Support & onboarding URL 
- Contact email and phone for enterprise sales

SKU & billing guidance (template and governance):
- Billing model: Usage-based (tokens/embedding-units) + optional monthly committed capacity SKU
- SKU naming pattern suggestion: RED-INF-PRT-[PARTNER_ABBR]-<SKU_TYPE>-<REGION> (e.g., RED-INF-PRT-ACME-COMMIT-US-WEST)
- Required metering events: request_start, tokens_consumed, embed_units, commit_capacity_consumed
- Invoices must show line-level breakdown by SKU and region; include a small sample invoice (attach to ticket ENG-2147)
- Trials: 30-day free credits or 100k tokens, mapped to temporary SKU RED-INF-TRIAL-PARTNER-XXXX
- Billing entitlement flow: marketplace purchase -> backend webhook -> create customer in Redwood billing -> enable SKU/entitlement in control plane

Technical acceptance criteria (minimal):
- API: Partner listing points to our public REST endpoint or to an integration-ready private endpoint pattern
- Auth: Support for marketplace-managed creds OR API-key provisioning via partner onboarding webhook
- VPC/private: Private control plane option documented with required network ranges, NAT/egress requirements, and required Bastion/peering steps
- KMS: Document KMS provider compatibility (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and required IAM roles/policies
- Observability: Instrumentation points for per-request tracing (trace_id, request_id) and metric hooks for latency/tokens
- Rate limiting: Default throttle policy for marketplace customers + ability to set per-customer limits
- Security review: Completed SAST report + pen test summary or attestation (or plan with dates)

Acceptance test matrix (examples):
- Provision a test customer with the committed capacity SKU -> run a 10k token workload -> verify committed throughput and token metering appear on dashboard and invoice line
- Create a private deployment in partner-managed VPC -> validate KMS key usage and audit logs for key operations
- Simulate region failure and ensure automatic fallback to alternate region variant within SLO bounds

Integration tickets to open (templates):
- ENG: Integrate marketplace webhook -> ticket body should include: partner marketplace webhook URL, expected webhook events, auth method, test webhook URL
- SRE: Add marketplace SKU billing rules and alerting thresholds
- SECURITY: Add partner to quarterly pentest scope and validate data flows for compliance
- DOCS: Create 1-pager marketplace quickstart + sample curl examples for hosted & private

Co-marketing and launch governance (who signs what):
- Legal: partner addendum (owner: Priya Singh)
- Sales: co-sell motion doc + naming of sales contacts (owner: Liam O'Connell)
- Marketing: landing page, announcement blog, joint webinar slot (owner: María Gómez)
- PM: product readiness checklist and feature flags gating launch (owner: Asha Patel)

Partner commitments we expect in parallel:
- Provide logo + brand guidelines (SVG preferred)
- Provide a sandbox account or test integration environment for validation
- Share a points-of-contact list (tech + GTM) and escalation path

Compliance & data residency notes (must be explicit in listing when relevant):
- If partner requires data residency, mark listing with region tags and provide steps to request private deployment in-region
- For EU and UK customers, list our SOC2 / ISO attestation references and where to request artifacts

Open questions / decisions required (TODOs):
- Pricing models: do we list both usage and committed capacity SKUs in the marketplace or present only a gateway SKU that maps client-side? (need finance input)
- Trials: default trial amount to offer via marketplace vs partner-managed (finance + sales to decide)
- Video: who will produce the 30s explainer? (marketing to confirm budget)

Launch timeline (rough):
- Week 0: Legal & billing SKU creation + sample invoice templates
- Week 1: Technical webhook + auth flows validated in sandbox
- Week 2: Asset submission (logos/screenshots/video) + docs drafted
- Week 3: Security attestation + final marketplace QA
- Week 4: Go-live (soft start for limited customers) -> monitor metrics for 7 days -> broad announcement

Owners and immediate next steps (this week):
- Asha Patel: finalize short & long listing copy and push to docs ticket DOCS-345
- Liam O'Connell: create the sales co-sell doc and register sales contacts in SFDC
- Priya Singh: circulate partner addendum draft for partner legal review
- María Gómez: draft announcement email and webinar outline; coordinate video production resource
- Daniel Okoye: create the ENG-2147 sandbox integration ticket and attach sample payloads

Notes to self:
- Keep copy concise and developer-focused; marketplace discovery favors short bullets + clear CTA (Get started / Request trial).
- Make sure billing SKU mapping is reversible and auditable; finance will require a mapping table for the entire first-quarter usage projection.

Appendix: sample curl (hosted API quickstart)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1", "input":"Summarize this document"}'

---
End of note. Keep iterating in this file. If we end up with minor copy variants, keep them as separate small files under go-to-market/copy-variants but reference here.
